source_boundary.preserved_question_intent: Design a platform that protects sensitive data both at rest and in transit, preserving the source-mentioned encryption/decryption, ciphertext storage, secure transport, KMS, crypto proxy/gateway, masking and domestic-commercial-cryptography concerns without inventing a company-specific topology, compliance level or algorithm mandate.

sources.title: RFC 9846: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3
anchors: TLS 1.3 protects client/server communication against eavesdropping, tampering and message forgery
RFC 9846 obsoletes RFC 8446 while retaining TLS version 1.3
the update is backward compatible while tightening and clarifying requirements

sources.title: RFC 9852 / BCP 195: New Protocols Using TLS Must Require TLS 1.3
anchors: new protocols that use TLS must require TLS 1.3
TLS 1.3 is the current baseline for new TLS-based protocol designs

sources.title: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5: Recommendation for Key Management
anchors: key-management guidance covers protection requirements for keying material and cryptographic information
key-management functions and lifecycle issues must be designed explicitly
access control, identity authentication, inventory and metadata protection are key-management concerns
sources.version_note: Rev. 5 remains the final publication; Rev. 6 is an initial public draft as of the check date and is not treated as the final normative baseline.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-130: A Framework for Designing Cryptographic Key Management Systems
anchors: a CKMS design must explicitly address key-management policies, procedures, components and metadata
access control, confidentiality, integrity, key metadata and source authentication are CKMS design topics
the design specification must document the required key-management topics rather than treating a KMS as a black box

sources.title: NIST SP 800-38D: GCM and GMAC
anchors: GCM is an authenticated-encryption-with-associated-data mode
authenticated encryption provides confidentiality plus authentication/integrity properties for protected data
the publication is under revision, so deployment profiles must track the current approved guidance rather than hard-code stale parameters
sources.version_note: The 2007 final remains published while NIST is revising SP 800-38D; current deployment parameters must be checked against the active NIST guidance at implementation time.

sources.title: 国家密码管理局：GB/T 39786-2021《信息安全技术 信息系统密码应用基本要求》正式发布
anchors: GB/T 39786-2021 is a foundational national standard for cryptographic application and security assessment
requirements span network and communications security as well as application and data security
cryptographic application includes both technical and management requirements

sources.title: 国家标准馆：GB/T 32907-2016 信息安全技术 SM4分组密码算法
anchors: GB/T 32907-2016 is listed as a current national standard
the standard specifies the SM4 block-cipher algorithm structure and implementation examples
SM4 is an algorithm primitive; a platform still needs an approved mode, key-management policy and deployment profile

sources.title: 国家标准馆：GB/T 32918.1-2016 信息安全技术 SM2椭圆曲线公钥密码算法 第1部分：总则
anchors: GB/T 32918.1-2016 defines the general foundation for the SM2 public-key cryptographic algorithm family
the source question's domestic-cryptography concern should be represented as a selectable policy/profile rather than by silently substituting one algorithm for every use case

claims.text: Transport protection and storage protection solve different boundaries. New TLS-based protocols should use TLS 1.3 as the transport baseline, while stored sensitive fields or objects need an explicit authenticated-encryption and key-management design; terminating TLS at a gateway does not by itself make downstream storage encrypted at rest.
source_anchors: TLS 1.3 protects client/server communication against eavesdropping, tampering and message forgery
new protocols that use TLS must require TLS 1.3

claims.text: A platform must treat key generation/import, identifiers and metadata, authorization, activation/rotation, revocation/destruction, backup/recovery and audit policy as first-class control-plane concerns. Application data should not embed or log plaintext key material merely because encryption is centralized behind an API.
source_anchors: key-management functions and lifecycle issues must be designed explicitly
access control, confidentiality, integrity, key metadata and source authentication are CKMS design topics

claims.text: For scalable data-at-rest protection, the design should separate data-encryption keys from higher-level key-encryption/master keys managed by the KMS/HSM boundary, record key/version metadata with ciphertext, and make rotation/re-encryption an explicit lifecycle workflow. The exact hierarchy and caching policy are deployment choices, not source facts.
source_anchors: protection requirements for keying material and cryptographic information
key metadata and key-management policies are CKMS design topics

claims.text: Sensitive-data storage should use an approved authenticated-encryption construction/profile where feasible so ciphertext manipulation is detected in addition to providing confidentiality. Algorithm, nonce/IV construction, tag length and version are part of the cryptographic profile and must follow current approved guidance rather than a hand-rolled scheme.
source_anchors: the publication is under revision, so deployment profiles must track the current approved guidance rather than hard-code stale parameters

claims.text: Where Chinese commercial-cryptography requirements apply, the platform should expose a policy/profile that can select the required domestic algorithms and compliant components, rather than scattering algorithm choices through application code. GB/T 39786-2021 covers cryptographic application requirements across communications plus application/data security, while SM2/SM4 standards define algorithm primitives; the exact mandated suite and assessment level must come from the target system's current regulatory profile.
source_anchors: requirements span network and communications security as well as application and data security
GB/T 32907-2016 is listed as a current national standard
GB/T 32918.1-2016 defines the general foundation for the SM2 public-key cryptographic algorithm family

claims.text: A crypto proxy/gateway can centralize policy enforcement, key access and migration, but it becomes a high-value trust boundary. The design still needs authenticated caller identity, least-privilege authorization to key/data domains, service-to-service transport protection, auditable key use and a clear rule for where plaintext is allowed to exist.

writer_constraints: Start by classifying data and trust boundaries: what is sensitive, who may decrypt it, whether searching/indexing on plaintext is required, and what compliance/cryptographic profile actually applies. Do not claim every field needs identical encryption semantics.
Draw separate data-at-rest and data-in-transit paths. Use current TLS 1.3 terminology from RFC 9846 rather than citing obsolete RFC 8446 as the current TLS 1.3 specification.

Make KMS/HSM/key lifecycle a control plane: key IDs/versions, authorization, rotation, revocation/destruction, backup/recovery and audit. Never put raw long-lived master keys in business configuration, logs or database rows.

Use envelope encryption as an architectural pattern: data is protected with a data key while higher-level keys stay in the managed key boundary; store ciphertext plus key/version/profile metadata so decryption and rotation are deterministic. Do not invent a universal DEK-per-row rule if data volume and threat model are unknown.

Prefer authenticated encryption for stored sensitive data and explicitly bind algorithm/mode/nonce/tag handling to a versioned crypto profile. Do not invent a custom cipher or describe bare ECB/CBC encryption as sufficient integrity protection.

Preserve the source's domestic-cryptography concern as a selectable compliance profile. Mention GB/T 39786-2021 plus SM2/SM4 only at the level supported by the frozen sources; do not claim a specific algorithm is legally mandatory for every Chinese deployment without the target system's current assessment profile.

Treat a crypto proxy/gateway as an optional centralization pattern with a trust/concentration tradeoff. Compare it with an SDK/sidecar/library approach and state how plaintext boundaries, caller identity, authorization, rate limiting and audit differ.

Separate encryption from masking/tokenization. Masking is an exposure-control/view concern and is not a replacement for cryptographic protection of stored sensitive data; if tokenization/FPE/searchable encryption is proposed, label it as a separate design choice requiring a specific query/use-case contract.

Cover availability and failure modes: KMS/HSM unavailable, key disabled/revoked, rotation half-complete, gateway overload, ciphertext/profile metadata corrupt, TLS/certificate failure and disaster recovery. Define fail-closed versus degraded behavior by data class; never silently fall back to plaintext.

Cover observability without leaking secrets: authorization denials, key-version usage, encryption/decryption latency/error rate, KMS/HSM saturation, rotation backlog, stale-key population, certificate/TLS errors and audit-event completeness. Explicitly prohibit logging plaintext sensitive values or raw key material.

Give a migration/rollout strategy: versioned ciphertext envelope, dual-read or controlled dual-write only where justified, background re-encryption, rollback to the previous supported profile, and reconciliation of rows/objects still using retired versions.

Do not fabricate company-specific HSM brand, compliance grade, QPS, key count, rotation period, incident metrics or personal production experience. Label any numeric sizing example as illustrative and require target-environment load/failure tests.
